sermon.title: The Gift of God's Word
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the word and the Spirit are synonymous (John 6:63), so the word gives new birth, growth and fruit. He shows the word working effectually in believers, the heart burning when Scripture is opened, the church’s call to preach the gospel the Lord confirms, and the blessing of reading, hearing, keeping and studying the Bible daily.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: his survey that 27 of 44 denominations accept homosexual members (unverified); founding details of the Affirming Pentecostal Church International (2010); the claim that “them” in Mark 16:20 is supplied/italicized; reading Romans 1:21 and 2 Timothy 3 as about believers (interpretation); 54% of Americans with STDs (unverified). Sensitive content: remark about someone saying God was black (1:55), homosexuality, Joel Osteen and the pope, incest/adultery remark.

faqs.question: Is Jesus God?
faqs.answer: Yes—the Word was God and became flesh.

faqs.question: How often should we feed on the word?
Can someone pray a magic prayer to fix our problems?
faqs.answer: No—you have to eat daily yourself; Sunday should confirm what you learned.

faqs.question: Is the Bible a book of myths?
faqs.answer: No—the word is living and powerful.

faqs.question: What is faith?
faqs.answer: He says faith is moral persuasion of what’s right, from the word.

faqs.question: Does God confirm opinions with signs?
faqs.answer: No—he confirms the preaching of the gospel.

faqs.question: Who stumbles over Jesus?
faqs.answer: Religious people who trust their opinions.

faqs.question: What should I read daily?
faqs.answer: A chapter of Proverbs and a page of Psalms, and read through the Bible.

faqs.question: Is rightly dividing the word difficult?
faqs.answer: No—the Bible is a book of wisdom and common sense.
